data.title: bn-2a3: M1.5.2.1 Preflight, locks and the frozen experiment
data.description: Review d165cd55323514a9012f8b385abf22a24f6367ca over base 54a567b79d7369cc2e2de4dd591b3eab239df04c. Verifier preflight persists keyed runs, takes deterministic pass/session/resource locks, validates pinned authority and passive Teapot gate plus dry-run accounting, retains/read-verifies the frozen experiment through Evidence, and links its artifact. Check concurrency, replay/start-boundary recovery, exact refusal mapping, zero target traffic, and SQLite migration/read compatibility.

data.body: [HIGH] Derive the ceiling plan from the frozen registered experiment; do not accept a free macro/session pair. PreflightRequest exposes macro_name and macro_session independently of the resolved FrozenExperiment, and LiveServices dry-runs exactly that caller-selected macro (lines 239-248). The only validation is that the selected session appears somewhere among either ordinary or verifier sessions (lines 464-488); no code binds the macro to the template recipe/operations, requires the verifier_session, or establishes that its request count covers all 12 registered recipe steps plus instrument-added login/retry sends. A caller can therefore name any existing low-count macro under an allowed session, pass preflight against a small remaining ceiling, then execute a larger frozen experiment that is only refused after partial target effects. This violates the bone’s dry-run-within-ceiling gate and the claim that every dependency is checked before target traffic. Please derive the dry-run operation(s), session(s), and total request bound from the compiled registry/frozen experiment (or freeze an exact registered execution plan), reject any mismatch with the registered typed code, and add a live regression where an unrelated one-request macro cannot admit a multi-request recipe under an insufficient ceiling.

[HIGH] The mutable-resource lock is scoped to the Teapot project, so it does not implement INV-18 across instrument/pass lanes that reach the same target resource. Two engagements can use different Teapot projects and different passes against the same target-side resource; their pass keys differ and `resource:{project}:{resource}` differs, so both preflights acquire leases and may plant/remove concurrently. The instrument project is a transport/custody namespace, not the identity of the mutable target resource. The final plan requires runs sharing a mutable resource not to overlap, and the earlier conflict-group definition also names target instance/reset domain independently of the instrument project. Please bind resource conflicts to a registered target-instance/reset/resource identity (or conservatively share the exact resource key across projects), freeze that identity, and add a derived-lock test with different pass digests and different projects that still conflicts on the same target resource. The existing test hand-constructs one common session string and cannot catch this derivation error.

[HIGH] Key the pass lock by stable pass identity/path, not the mutable content digest. `pass:<digest>` lets an already-running lease on revision A coexist with a newly admitted run on revision B of the same pass reference/file, because the changed digest produces another flock file. Those runs share the pass ledger/spender and violate the explicit “runs against one pass are serialized” requirement exactly during amendment/revocation windows, when serialization matters most. It also needlessly aliases two distinct pass instances with byte-identical declarations. Use the registered PassRef and/or canonical approved pass-file identity as the conflict key while retaining the digest check for authority, then add a concurrency case with one pass identity/path and two revisions/digests that cannot overlap.

[MEDIUM] This target-sink witness is disconnected from the system under test, so it cannot establish the acceptance claim it names. `TargetSink` is a private UnixDatagram pair; neither `prepare`, `FakeServices`, `LiveServices`, Teapot, nor any spawned process receives its sender/address. `prove_live` only proves the test can send its own control, and `assert_quiet` must remain quiet even if production preflight sends real HTTP elsewhere. The test also executes only missing-slots and changed-pass paths; the separate mapping test constructs error values without driving gate, accounting, evidence, revision, replay, session, or lock failures. Please replace/supplement this with a composed pinned LiveServices run whose Teapot target is the owned loopback sink and inject each reachable refusal after declaration, asserting its exact frozen code and zero target requests. Keep the existing call-log checks as useful ordering evidence, but do not call the detached datagram proof non-vacuous.

[HIGH] A process crash drops the only conflict state and permits an unsafe overlapping run after the execution-start boundary. The lease is just kernel flock ownership; SIGKILL closes the descriptors, and the empty lock files retain no owning run or durable state. `prepare` then checks only the new request’s own `RunState`/steps (lines 404-408), never another run that previously held the same pass/session/resource keys. Reproduction: A prepares and holds the lease, persists step intent, dispatches (the Teapot job may outlive the CLI), then is killed; B acquires the now-free flock and passes preflight while A’s effect is unknown/in flight. Plan §7.5 explicitly says unknown-effect runs block conflicts until disposition, a killed verifier job may continue, and lock expiry alone never proves it stopped. Persist conflict claims keyed to the run before/with acquisition, retain enough ownership metadata after process death, and on takeover consult the run/step state so only a declared run with no start intent can be safely reclaimed; unresolved/started owners must return CONFLICTING_RUN until reconciliation/disposition. Add a subprocess SIGKILL test after persisted step intent plus an independently running sink/job, not only the current unwind-before-work release test.

data.reason: Four HIGH blockers: durable crash-safe conflict claims are absent; ceiling admission is based on an unbound caller-selected macro/session; pass locks use mutable digests instead of stable pass identity; mutable-resource locks are incorrectly scoped to instrument project. One MEDIUM: the claimed network-sink/typed-refusal acceptance test is disconnected and incomplete. See open threads th-185i88, th-90b3zn, th-3hc52l, th-3mejhr, and th-3mnxe4.

data.body: Fixed in dc172be: preflight now transactionally claims the complete durable conflict set after request acceptance and before any adapter/effect boundary. Started or unknown-effect owners remain blocking after SIGKILL; claims release only for a declared run with no step intent or within a fully resolved terminal transition. Added atomic partial-unwind, idempotency, terminal recovery, and cross-process SIGKILL coverage with an independently surviving job that reaches the connected TCP sink while a competing prepare returns CONFLICTING_RUN.

Fixed in dc172be: removed caller-selected macro/session from PreflightRequest. The exact frozen template/recipe now derives the registered plant macro, owner verifier session, expected plant request count, and conservative full-recipe send/login/retry bound; accounting cross-checks the observed macro count and the full bound against remaining capacity. Added the unrelated-macro and caller-undercount regression plus pinned live coverage.

Fixed in dc172be: pass conflicts are keyed by the registered stable PassRef, while the pinned digest remains an independent authority check. Added a derived-key/flock regression proving the same pass identity conflicts across changed digests/revisions and distinct pass identities do not alias solely on identical bytes.

Fixed in dc172be: mutable target resources now use a project-independent resource:<registered-resource> conflict key; Teapot sessions retain their exact project-scoped native identities. Added a two-project/two-pass derived-lock regression proving the same target resource still conflicts.

Fixed in dc172be: removed the disconnected datagram claim and added a composed pinned LiveServices test using the real pinned Teapot and Investigation adapters against an owned TCP target. Active-edit refusal and successful preflight both produce zero target requests, while a positive control through the same bound Teapot macro/session produces two requests. Added driven table coverage for all reachable gate, accounting, evidence, authority/revision, replay/session/lock mappings with exact registered codes and claim cleanup checks.

Verified at exact target dc172be: durable conflict-set ownership is committed before adapters, record_step requires the claim, unresolved/unknown owners survive SIGKILL, and only unstarted or fully resolved terminal owners are reclaimable. The focused cross-process test passed with a surviving TCP job reaching the owned sink while the contender returned CONFLICTING_RUN; atomic partial-claim and terminal-release cases also passed.

Verified at exact target dc172be: PreflightRequest no longer accepts macro/session inputs. The frozen compiled template derives plant plus the owner verifier session, cross-checks the live macro dry-run count of 2, and requires the conservative full-recipe bound of 32 against pass-wide remaining capacity. The unrelated one-request macro and insufficient-capacity regressions passed, as did the pinned two-request positive control.

Verified at exact target dc172be: the conflict key is pass:<PassRef>, independent of mutable digest, while authority still checks the pinned digest separately. The changed-digest/same-reference derived-key and flock regression passed.

Verified at exact target dc172be: mutable resource ownership is now resource:<registered-resource> without Teapot project scoping; only native session keys remain project scoped. The two-project/two-pass shared-resource derived-lock regression passed.

Verified at exact target dc172be: the detached datagram witness is gone. The pinned LiveServices test used the frozen Teapot and Investigation binaries against one owned TCP target: active-edit refusal and successful preflight produced zero requests, then the same bound Teapot/project/macro/session positive control produced exactly two. The driven refusal table and exact code assertions also passed.

data.body: [HIGH] The engagement-revision gate does not compare against the current engagement head, so an unstarted request-key replay can preflight successfully after the engagement changed. Reproduction against exact dc172be in a disposable test: accept the verify key at revision 1, append manifest revision 2, then call prepare with the same key and old ManifestRevision. declare_request replays the stored revision-1 acceptance; line 426 only compares that stored 1 to the same caller-supplied old manifest 1, so admission, Evidence record/readback, and success all occur instead of REVISION_CONFLICT. This can run the frozen recipe under stale sessions, resource identity, effect limits, or other operator settings. Read and compare the current engagement revision after conflict acquisition and before any adapter call (with an ordering strategy that closes the check/use race), return the registered revision code on mismatch, and add this lost-response/replay-after-amendment regression.

[HIGH] Migration 009 creates empty conflict tables, but the new record_step and record_run guards treat every keyed run without a conflict row as an illegal start. Every pre-009 keyed run necessarily has no row. Exact-target disposable reproduction: construct a valid schema-v7 database with a declared keyed run, open it through Store::open so 008/009 migrate, then record its first step; record_step returns StoreError::Conflict. A legacy run that already has steps is worse: claim_conflicts rejects nonzero steps, while record_run with bundled steps is also blocked, so its effects cannot be reconciled or finalized after upgrade. Preserve upgrade compatibility while conservatively representing legacy ownership (or explicitly distinguish legacy runs from new preflight runs), and add v7 migration cases for unstarted, started/unknown, and terminal keyed runs.

data.reason: Exact target dc172be still admits an unstarted keyed replay after the engagement head advances (th-3946s5), and migration 009 bricks post-upgrade step/outcome recording for pre-existing keyed runs that have no conflict rows (th-3ba6dl). Both exact-target adversarial regressions reproduced; the five prior findings were independently verified and resolved.

data.body: Fixed in 83f0f53. Conflict acquisition now uses one immediate SQLite transaction to compare the request acceptance revision with the current MAX(engagement_revisions.revision) before installing the durable claim; a stale replay returns REVISION_CONFLICT before any adapter. append_manifest now checks the active durable claim in its own ordered write transaction, so either amendment commits first and admission observes the new head, or admission commits first and the amendment is refused until terminal/recovery release. The checked regression drives both orderings and asserts zero adapter calls on stale replay.

Fixed in 83f0f53. Migration 009 now records every pre-existing keyed run, installs a conservative legacy barrier for every unresolved one, and leaves only fully resolved terminal runs unclaimed. An explicitly resumed unstarted legacy run converts atomically to exact derived keys and a failed preflight restores its legacy barrier; any other new exact admission remains globally blocked while unresolved legacy identity is unknowable. record_step and record_run reconciliation remain available for migrated unstarted and started/unknown runs, terminal resolution releases the barrier, and resolved terminal compatibility permits only already-existing settled steps. Three schema-v7 migration regressions cover unstarted, started/unknown, and terminal cases, including rejection of a new terminal step and a positive global-block witness.

Verified fixed at exact target 83f0f53bac060d1510d0b5996fb79b0418728f58. claim_conflicts now reads the accepted request revision and current engagement head in the same IMMEDIATE transaction before any claim insert/reclaim; mismatch returns RevisionConflict. The focused stale-key regression passed, and the clean exact-source core suite passed 150/150 runnable unit tests (2 helper-only ignored) plus integration/doc tests. I also inspected the opposite ordering test: a held successful claim fences a later manifest append. Resolving this thread; a separate manifest-fence liveness defect is being filed independently.

data.reason: Exact target 83f0f53 atomically rejects stale accepted revisions before claim mutation; focused and full exact-source tests pass.

data.body: Still blocking at exact target 83f0f53bac060d1510d0b5996fb79b0418728f58. The single-run migration cases are repaired, but the global legacy barrier cannot make progress with two ordinary v7 declared/no-step keyed runs. In a disposable exact-target adversarial test, v9 migration installed one legacy set for each run; claim_conflicts for the first returned CONFLICTING_RUN because the second legacy set exists, and claim_conflicts for the second returned the same because the first exists. Thus neither definitionally unstarted/safe-to-reclaim owner can resume or convert, and new exact admission remains globally blocked (including unrelated engagements). This is a deterministic migration denial, not a transient lock. Classify/reclaim safe zero-step legacy owners or provide an ordered recovery path that provably makes progress; add 2+ owner and cross-engagement migration coverage. Leaving this thread open.

[HIGH] The manifest fence converts a safe pre-start crash/drop into an unbounded amendment denial and also blocks the documented engagement-stop path. A successful prepare installs an exact durable set; dropping or killing Prepared before record_step releases only the live flocks. append_manifest then rejects the old unstarted/reclaimable set, so the engagement cannot advance until a future conflicting admission happens to reclaim it or an out-of-band release is invoked. Disposable exact-target reproduction: prepare succeeds; drop Prepared; assert zero steps and conflicts_held=true; append revision 2 returns RevisionConflict. The same predicate rejects every amendment throughout an active/unknown run, while plan 7.1 requires an engagement stop to block new runs immediately and request cancellation of the active one. Preserve the atomic check/use ordering, but provide a safe stop/amendment path and deterministic pre-start crash reclamation; cover drop/SIGKILL plus active and unknown owners in both orderings.

data.reason: Exact target 83f0f53bac060d1510d0b5996fb79b0418728f58 remains unsafe: th-3ba6dl proves a deterministic multi-owner v7 migration deadlock/global admission denial, and th-97npmp proves stale unstarted claims plus active/unknown claims deny engagement amendments and the required stop path. th-3946s5 stale-revision admission is fixed and resolved.

data.body: Fixed in a890368. Migration 009 no longer installs barriers for schema-v7 declared zero-step runs, so multiple owners across engagements can independently resume into exact disjoint key sets. A direct legacy first step transactionally establishes one conservative global barrier; any started or unknown owner remains blocking until terminal reconciliation, while safe zero-step exact claims are reclaimed atomically. Failed preflight release deletes the safe claim rather than recreating a mutually blocking legacy barrier. Regression coverage proves two-owner cross-engagement progress, ordered direct-start exclusion, exact-claim reclamation, started/unknown retention, and resolved-terminal compatibility.

Fixed in a890368 with an explicit lifecycle. Prepared::abandon consumes a pre-start admission and releases its durable claim only after Store verifies zero steps. Ordinary append atomically reclaims dropped or SIGKILLed zero-step owners, while append_stop_manifest advances the stop revision, retains every started or unknown claim, and marks each owner cancel_requested for the execution/recovery path. Later stale record_run updates preserve that cancellation flag monotonically. Both append and step writers use immediate transactions, so amendment-first makes the late step fail and step-first retains the durable fence. Regressions cover drop, explicit abandon, cross-process SIGKILL, both writer orders, observed and unknown active owners, cancellation persistence, and ordinary-amendment refusal after start.

Still blocking at exact target a89036881918074fcc1ac452f9a84201fdb1bc21. The original two-owner deadlock is fixed: four migration-v9 regressions pass and the new no-barrier/direct-start scheme serializes two owners and releases after terminal settlement. However, the new direct legacy start bypasses the engagement-revision fence. Disposable exact-target reproduction: migrate a valid v7 declared/no-step keyed run (no barrier), append_stop_manifest so the engagement advances from revision 1 to 2, then call record_step on the migrated run; it succeeds, installs a legacy barrier, and records Unknown under the stale pre-stop acceptance. install_legacy_start_barrier checks legacy identity and unstarted state but never compares request_keys.engagement_revision with the current head. Thus amendment-first does not make this late legacy start fail, and a stop can be crossed. Perform the accepted/current revision check in the same IMMEDIATE first-step transaction and add ordinary/stop amendment-first direct-start regressions. Leaving this thread open.

Still blocking at exact target a89036881918074fcc1ac452f9a84201fdb1bc21. Prepared abandon, dropped/SIGKILL zero-step reclamation, active/unknown claim retention, and monotonic cancel_requested all pass focused/full tests. But append_stop_manifest does not durably mark the engagement stopped: it only appends a normal engagement revision, labels the audit event engagement.stop, and marks owners that already hold conflict rows. Disposable exact-target reproduction: append stop revision 2, declare a brand-new keyed run afterward; acceptance binds engagement_revision=2, then claim_conflicts succeeds and holds the new run. No admission path consults a stopped state, so the documented guarantee that stop blocks new runs is absent (and a later ordinary amendment can likewise proceed when no active owner remains). Persist a stop fence consulted atomically by request acceptance/replay and claim acquisition, with an explicit resume transition if intended; regress stop-before-declare and stop-before-claim. Leaving this thread open.

data.reason: Exact target a89036881918074fcc1ac452f9a84201fdb1bc21 remains unsafe. th-3ba6dl: migrated v7 direct first-step admission can start after an ordinary/stop amendment because it skips accepted-vs-current revision validation. th-97npmp: stop is not persisted as an admission fence, so a brand-new request accepted after the stop can claim and start. Intended multi-owner progress, Prepared reclaim, active/unknown retention, and monotonic cancellation otherwise validate.

data.body: Fixed at bebce4e: engagement_stops is now durable admission state, installed transactionally with append_stop_manifest and consulted by fresh declare, idempotent replay, exact claim, and migrated direct first-step admission. Ordinary amendments preserve the fence; append_resume_manifest is the explicit ordered transition that reclaims only zero-step owners and refuses active/unknown owners before deleting the fence. Regressions cover stop-before-new-request, preaccepted-before-stop, no row/claim/adapter traffic on refusal, amendment persistence, explicit resume, and retained active/unknown cancellation.

Fixed at bebce4e: legacy direct-first-step and normal exact-claim admission now share one Immediate-transaction predicate that atomically cross-checks the accepted request revision against the current engagement head and the durable stop fence before installing any barrier/claim or recording a step. The schema-v10 regression covers both ordinary and stop amendments and proves RevisionConflict with no claim/step; multi-owner progress, active/unknown reconciliation, explicit abandon, and terminal release remain green.

Verified fixed at exact target bebce4e302f24dfce319567f69842ba9636dc6a6 over base 6ac274005cd95bfc6bb26f668bd645aff2b368ce. A migrated direct first-step now calls accepted_run_admission inside the same IMMEDIATE transaction that installs the global legacy barrier and step; both ordinary-amendment-first and stop-first stale acceptances return RevisionConflict with no claim. Five focused migration-v10 tests pass, including multi-owner cross-engagement progress, direct-start ordering, started/unknown reconciliation, terminal release, and resolved-terminal compatibility. The post-sync 008 lead surface followed by renamed 009/010 migrations was also independently exercised from a populated schema-v8 lead database; every new lead field survived and schema advanced to 10. Resolving.

data.reason: Exact bebce4e atomically fences stale legacy direct starts while preserving multi-owner progress and the corrected post-sync migration lineage.

data.body: Verified fixed at exact target bebce4e302f24dfce319567f69842ba9636dc6a6. engagement_stops is now durable FK-backed admission state. New acceptance, identical replay, exact claim, and migrated direct-start paths all consult it; ordinary amendments preserve it, and only append_resume_manifest deletes it. The focused stop test passed, and an independent exact-target probe proved an identical pre-stop key is refused through stop plus an ordinary amendment, then becomes readable only after explicit resume. Active/unknown owners retain claims and monotonic cancel_requested; Prepared abandon/drop/SIGKILL reclaim and terminal release all pass the full suite. Resolving.

data.reason: Exact bebce4e persists stop admission, orders stop/resume against claims, and permits admission only through the explicit resume transition.
